clue.text: A pal must have short garments in a UAE state

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter of the following word goes

blocks.note: taken as written
a bud, or buddy, is a friend
a habit is a set of clothing, as worn by a monk or nun or for riding

explanation.surface: A friend arriving in the Emirates had better bring some skimpy clothes for the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: HABIT loses its last letter, and A, BUD and HABI run together as ABU DHABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the largest of the seven emirates making up the United Arab Emirates, and holds its capital.

clue.text: London theatre god

blocks.note: first meaning: a theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End
second meaning: the Greek god of the sun, music and poetry

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a star of the London stage; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apollo is a West End theatre, and Apollo is a major deity of Greek and Roman mythology.

clue.text: It's difficult, apparently, making one apprehensive

definitions.note: cryptic: read as UN-EASY, not easy

blocks.note: first meaning, read jokily: something difficult is not easy
second meaning: anxious, worried

explanation.surface: A difficult situation is bound to make anyone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags the playful reading: split the answer as UN-EASY, which is literally what difficult means.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uneasy feels anxious about what might happen, the same feeling as apprehensive.

clue.text: Common people voting in Orkney island reportedly circle one

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the place name is taken for how it sounds

blocks.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands, off northern Scotland
a poll is a vote
the letter O is circle-shaped
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ordinary islanders voting in Orkney, each circling one candidate on the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is an island in Orkney, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek phrase for 'the many', used in English for the masses or ordinary people.

clue.text: Largest being wild animals

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The biggest creatures living wild in nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animals' reads as one phrase, but wild is the anagram signal and animals alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengal tigers are big cats of India and Bangladesh, so they are examples of animals.

clue.text: Girl, good liar, unusually, about love

indicators.note: letters arranged unusually are not in their normal order, so the word is rearranged
the rearranged word goes about, that is around, the next piece

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written, to be rearranged
love is nil in tennis, and nil looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl who is, unusually for a good liar, talking about love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a tennis score of nil looks like a zero; it sits inside the rearranged liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria is a woman's first name, so it stands for a girl as crossword definitions often do.

clue.text: Romance at home, so stay longer beneath the sheets

blocks.note: to romance is to tell fanciful stories, that is to lie
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A romantic night at home, so the couple stay in bed late next morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Romance looks like a love affair but is the verb meaning to invent stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in is to stay in bed later than usual in the morning, still under the covers.

clue.text: Check remainder before wet weather

blocks.note: the rest is what remains
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Check what remains to be done before the rain sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the first piece ahead of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, which is what restrain means.

clue.text: Dog show, first in Eden Valley?

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, taken on its own

blocks.note: to air something is to show it publicly
the opening letter of Eden
a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: A dog show held, perhaps for the first time, in the Eden Valley of Cumbria.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden Valley is in Cumbria, England, and Airedale is a Yorkshire valley that gave the terrier its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Compliant theologian carrying one in on time

indicators.note: a word carrying something holds it inside itself
one thing in another is placed inside it, so the theologian goes inside the next word

blocks.note: first letter of the word on, which is split around the theologian
the Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon monk and theologian
I is the Roman numeral for one
second letter of the word on, closing round the theologian
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A docile churchman carries someone in, right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside BEDE to make BEDIE, that sits inside ON to make OBEDIEN, and T finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A compliant person does what they are told, which is what being obedient means.

clue.text: Tricky question, last of four on card

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone
in an across clue, one piece placed on another is written after it

blocks.note: to card wool is to comb out its fibres, which is also called teasing it
the final letter of four

explanation.surface: A card game question so hard it stumps the last of four players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on card' means the letter goes after the card word. Carding and teasing both mean combing out fibres of wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or brain-teaser, a question designed to be difficult to answer.

clue.text: Publisher's job for old fellow connected with English university

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
O is the abbreviation for old
F is the abbreviation for fellow
Reading is a town in Berkshire with a university

explanation.surface: A publishing job for an old university fellow in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Checking proofs for errors before printing is a standard task in a publishing house.

clue.text: Catch girl close to gazebo

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so take only its final letter

blocks.note: a lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland
the final letter of gazebo

explanation.surface: Someone trying to catch a girl standing near a garden gazebo.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope, so the verb matches catch.

clue.text: A D.H. Lawrence novel, or Dr No as a novel

indicators.note: the last word here means new or original, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a Lawrence novel, or perhaps the Bond novel Dr No, to be rated as a novel?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters are 'or Dr No as a', with 'as' among them: nine letters that rearrange to the title. The word novel does two different jobs in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's Rod is a 1922 novel by D.H. Lawrence, named after the flute its hero carries.

clue.text: Painting of smooth US president and philosopher

blocks.note: a flat surface is smooth and level
Gerald Ford was the 38th US president
John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century English philosopher

explanation.surface: A portrait painted of a smooth-talking American president standing beside a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Flatford Mill is in Suffolk, England; John Constable painted it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatford Mill is the title of a famous 1817 Constable landscape, so the name stands for a painting.

clue.text: Gangster's crazy speed on road abroad

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters next to it are jumbled
abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered too

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mobster driving at a crazy speed on a road overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate shuffles, one for each word, with 'on' setting the second after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, violent criminal, especially in the Wild West, much like a gangster.

clue.text: Unconventional youngsters with no money turned up after 'Live Aid', initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take only the first letter
in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
the first letter of Aid
skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Penniless young rebels turned up at the Live Aid concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Live Aid was the 1985 charity concert; here the two words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were young bohemians of the 1950s and 60s who rejected conventional society.

clue.text: A leader, inaccurate about western US state

indicators.note: something inaccurate is not right, so the letters are put in a different order
the words go about, that is around, the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
W is the abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: A leader making false claims about the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: W joins the letters of 'A leader', and all eight are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a small state on the US east coast, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: DJ just died in entrance?

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the letter goes within the following word

blocks.note: even, as in fair or just
D is the abbreviation for died
ingress is a way in, an entrance

explanation.surface: Did a disc jockey just die in the doorway?
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like disc jockey but here means dinner jacket, which counts as formal evening wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket, or DJ, is formal wear for evening events, so it is an example of evening dress.

clue.text: So I am desperately after motorway plant

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: M is used for motorway, as in the M1
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stranded by the motorway, desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged letters behind M. British motorways are numbered with M, as in the M25.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a plant with fluffy yellow flowers, and also the sensitive plant whose leaves fold when touched.

clue.text: Witness change in state trooper's leader

indicators.note: a change in something alters it, so the following word is rearranged
a word's leader is the letter at its front

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first letter of trooper

explanation.surface: A witness to a state trooper's change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State trooper' reads as one American phrase, but state is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to sign to confirm it is genuine, which is also to attest it.

clue.text: Pastry brought round to character over in restaurant

indicators.note: something brought round is turned to face the other way, so read the word backwards
turned over means flipped, so this word too is read from the end

blocks.note: a tart is a pastry case with a filling
taken as written
an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A pastry carried round to a character dining in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, so it is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Jeering remark beginning to trouble uncle's wife

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken alone

blocks.note: the first letter of trouble
an uncle's wife is an aunt

explanation.surface: A mocking remark is the start of trouble with an uncle's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A taunt is a provoking or mocking jibe, a jeering remark.

clue.text: Live with chauvinist - seconds out!

indicators.note: something sent out is removed, so the letter named is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a sexist is a male chauvinist
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Living with a male chauvinist calls for a boxing referee: seconds out!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds out' is the boxing call to clear the ring before a round; here it removes S from SEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To live is to be alive, and to exist means the same as a verb.

clue.text: He died flying, one tenor starved of oxygen

indicators.note: something starved of an item is going without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Enrico Caruso was a famous Italian tenor
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An airman or singer who perished in flight, starved of oxygen at altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: CARUSO loses its O, and I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings, which melted, and he fell to his death.

clue.text: Apron-like garment found in shop in a forecourt

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is sitting inside it, running across the word breaks

blocks.note: the letters run across shop, in, a and forecourt

explanation.surface: An apron-style garment on sale in a shop on a garage forecourt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless garment worn over clothes to protect them, much like an apron.

clue.text: Bloodhound in Olivier/Caine film

blocks.note: first meaning: a detective, someone who tracks down criminals
second meaning: the 1972 thriller starring Laurence Olivier and Michael Caine

explanation.surface: A tracker dog appearing in a classic Olivier and Caine thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloodhound looks like the dog, but it is the informal word for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, informally called a bloodhound, and Sleuth is also the title of the 1972 film.

clue.text: In the dark I allow not one inside

indicators.note: a piece put inside another sits within its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
to grant is to allow or permit
no, as in no person, means not one

explanation.surface: Kept in the dark, I refuse to let a single one in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not one' reads as part of the surface refusal but supplies a piece, placed after the first letter of the allow word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge, which is what ignorant means.
